newsitem.title: INDIA: India decides to keep fresh wheat purchase on hold.
newsitem.headline: India decides to keep fresh wheat purchase on hold.

text.p: India's State Trading Corporation (STC) has decided to keep on hold the purchase of one million tonnes of wheat out of two million it was authorised to import during 1997/98 (April-March), a senior STC official said on Thursday.
"The cabinet has told us specifically not to buy the one million tonnes," the STC official, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters.
STC has already contracted to buy one million tonnes of wheat from Australia during the year.
The official said STC had told the Australian authorities that India would take delivery of the one million tonnes only after it was cleaned of weeds.
"We have told Australia to clean it up so that we do not contravene any laws of the land," the official said. "Discussions are on."
The wheat is due for shipment from August.
The Economic Times newspaper said on Thursday the government, acting on the opinion of the Agriculture Ministry, had cleared the wheat imports.
But STC officials said they had yet to receive clearance from the government.

STC had earlier contracted to import 1.75 million tonnes of wheat after India authorised the import of two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March) to build stocks and check rising domestic prices.
Out of this, 1.3 million tonnes was purchased from Australia and the remainder from Argentina and Canada. The entire quantity had been shipped and distributed in India.
Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said in June that weeds were detected in wheat shipments from Australia but they were not harmful.

An Indian delegation visited Australia in June to discuss the presence of weeds in its wheat exports to India and new specifications for further exports with the Australian Wheat Board and the Australian Plant Quarantine Inspection Service.
Analysts said the weed-infected wheat was not harmful if consumed, but would yield a smaller crop if used for sowing.
The STC official said Australia would need to pay for cleaning the wheat.

India's state agencies had until Wednesday bought nearly 9.2 million tonnes of wheat for sale in 1997/98 (April-March) compared with 8.2 million in the previous season, a senior Food Corporation of India official said.
